Subject: Fee floor operational playbook & order form markup

Mateo —

Thanks for the call last week. Attached is Novus's v3 redline to the order form plus a short note on how we'd like the fee floor/stabilizer to operate during burst and scale events. High-level items: 

- We propose a soft floor set at 60% of committed monthly units with a true-up quarterly (to avoid short-term volatility).
- We want an operational playbook (Annex A) that specifies how bursts are classified and how credits are applied for unbilled bursts.
- We added confidentiality carveouts around billing calculations and requested a mutual audit right limited to one event per 12 months.

Would appreciate Redwood's proposed edits on the calculation language for the floor (Section 3 of Exhibit B) and the proposed Annex A. We can be flexible on the exact percentage but need clarity on the measurement window and fallback during capacity shortages.

Attachments: Novus_Redline_v3.docx (redline), pricing-playbook-diff.txt (playbook diff)

Regards,
Samantha Reed
VP Finance — Novus Analytics

Subject: Re: Fee floor operational playbook & order form markup

Samantha —

Thanks for the redline and the playbook diff. Read through quickly — helpful to see the scenarios called out. A few asks from our side before formal legal markup: 

- Definition clarity: please confirm the lookback window you used to compute the 60% (rolling 30-day vs calendar month). That affects how our autoscale credits interact.
- Stabilizer trigger: we prefer a tiered true-up (monthly monitoring, quarterly settlement) but need firm caps on the quarterly true-up amount to limit financial exposure. Would Novus accept a quarterly cap equal to 40% of the committed monthly units?
- Burst carveout language: we need Annex A to define "burst event" precisely (duration, threshold) and include telemetry sources Redwood will accept for validation.

Looping in Laura and Markus for legal redline. Karthik, can you confirm this aligns with the commercial commitment on the deal? Marissa — can your ops team draft a short MOP (method of performance) for Annex A showing the process flow we've discussed?

If we can align on these items by close of business Wednesday (03/24) we can consolidate and send back to you for final review.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Subject: Re: Fee floor operational playbook & order form markup

Matt (cc Mateo) / Samantha —

Thanks for the materials — I reviewed Novus's v3 redline. High-level legal comments: 

1) Move calculation mechanics for the floor out of the core T&Cs and into Exhibit B (Order Schedule) with a cross-reference in the MSA. That keeps the main agreement readable and lets both parties iterate on the numeric parameters in the schedule.

2) For the true-up cap: suggest we define the cap as a percentage of the "committed monthly units" with an explicit formula. Proposed wording (tracked in the attached snippet): "Quarterly true-up liability shall not exceed 40% of the average committed monthly units over the prior calendar quarter." This ties to a clear calculation and limits exposure.

3) Define "Burst Event" in Annex A. Proposed parameters: minimum 15-minute sustained delta > 3x baseline for at least two discrete occurrences in a 30-day window. Include telemetry sources: Redwood per-request logs, Novus-provided usage reports, and a mutually-agreed time-series metric (e.g., tokens/sec).

4) Audit right: Redwood can accept a mutual audit right but proposes a narrower scope: one audit per 12 months, notice 30 days in advance, and costs borne by the requesting party unless material noncompliance is found.

5) Confidentiality around billing calculations is acceptable, but we need to preserve Redwood's right to use aggregated de-identified metrics for internal optimization. We'll propose a carveout limiting disclosure only to the contracting parties and required auditors.

I've attached a short markup snippet (inline) and will draft the consolidated redline once we agree on the numeric parameters and definitions.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fee floor operational playbook & order form markup

Markus —

Thanks for the concrete edits; those read clean. Two quick follow-ups from Novus: 

- The proposed "2x occurrence in 30 days" burst definition is fine, but Novus asks we allow for a one-off emergency spike caused by platform migration without triggering the true-up (we can include a force majeure carveout for planned migrations with 14 days' notice).
- Audit costs: Novus prefers cost-sharing for audits unless there is clear billing error >5% in which case Redwood bears costs.

We are flexible on the aggregated metric carveout language if Redwood acknowledges that any aggregated data shared externally will be anonymized and cannot be reverse-engineered to Novus's unit counts.

Also — happy to do a 30-minute call Tuesday (03/23) to resolve the remaining open bullets. I've prepared a short confidentiality excerpt to propose (attached).

Samantha
VP Finance — Novus Analytics

Team / Samantha —

Quick summary and asks after Markus's notes: 

- Agree to move the detailed calculation language to Exhibit B and add Annex A as the operational playbook.
- Karthik: confirm commercial acceptance of a quarterly true-up cap equal to 40% of committed monthly units. If Novus refuses, let me know the max they'd accept so we can escalate.
- Marissa: please draft Annex A (MOP) with the telemetry sources Marcus listed and a proposed verification runbook. Keep it short (1 page).
- Laura/Markus: capture the audit cost split language: request Redwood to accept cost-sharing unless Bill Error >5% (then Redwood pays).

Timeline: consolidate redline by 03/24 EOD so we can route to Novus procurement and target signature week of 03/29.

Next steps: Karthik to confirm by EOD; Marissa to send draft Annex A by EOD tomorrow; Laura/Markus to produce consolidated redline.

Thanks —
Mateo

Folks —

Attached is Redwood's consolidated redline (Redwood_Consolidated_Redline_v1.docx) and a proposed Annex A (Operational_Playbook_AnnexA_v1.pdf). Key changes incorporated: 

- Floor calculation moved to Exhibit B with explicit formula and examples.
- Quarterly true-up cap language added (matches Markus's suggested formula).
- Burst Event definition added to Annex A with telemetry sources and verification runbook.
- Audit clause narrowed: one audit per 12 months; requesting party pays unless variance >5%.
- Confidentiality carveout tightened to allow Redwood to use only aggregated, de-identified metrics for internal performance tuning.

If Novus is comfortable we'll prepare a clean order schedule and attach the two exhibits for signature. Otherwise, propose we escalate to a short call tomorrow with legal and procurement.
